log.text: Light Screen up on P1's side
Light Screen ended on P1's side

decisions.rationale: Lead Rotom-Wash + Klefki to handle sand mode: Klefki sets Reflect/Light Screen with Prankster, Rotom-Wash threatens Tyranitar and Excadrill with Hydro Pump (2x) while Levitate dodges High Horsepower. Back Dragapult for Ghost-killing speed and Incineroar for Intimidate cycling, Fake Out disruption, and Darkest Lariat into Gholdengo/Gengar. Screens up first gives the back line longevity against spread Rock Slide and special spam.

Lead Gengar-Mega + Houndoom: Gengar-Mega Taunts Klefki before screens and Shadow Tag traps; Houndoom Flash Fire absorbs Rotom WoW (G1 lesson) and threatens Dragapult/Metagross. Back Tyranitar + Excadrill: keep TTar healthy for late-game sand+Rock Slide flinches, Excadrill Focus Sash Sand Rush as wincon once sand is up.
decisions.notebook: G2 lead: Gengar-Mega + Houndoom, back Tyranitar + Excadrill. Key: Mega Gengar turn 1 for Shadow Tag + Taunt Klefki before screens. Houndoom is Rotom-W WoW absorber via Flash Fire. Bring Tyranitar in mid/late for sand to enable Excadrill sweep. Watch for Metagross-Mega (130-162 Spe) outspeeding Excadrill in sand (140) if max invested — Houndoom Flamethrower is the answer. If opponent brings Corviknight G2, Tyranitar Rock Slide + Houndoom Flamethrower cover it. Dragapult at 178-213 Spe outspeeds Gengar-Mega (~200) if max invested — respect this speed tier.

selection: Light Screen (your side, including ally Rotom-Wash)
decisions.rationale: Switch Rotom-Wash to Incineroar to dodge the potential Mega Gengar Shadow Tag trap and bring in a Dark-type that resists or is immune to every attack both foes carry (Flamethrower/Dark Pulse/Energy Ball all NVE, Shadow Ball immune). Intimidate provides minor utility. Klefki sets Prankster Light Screen at +1 priority before any foe move or Taunt, halving special damage for 8 turns with Light Clay. This turn 1 establishes a durable defensive shell while preserving Rotom-Wash for later.

Mega Evolve Gengar for Shadow Tag and Taunt Klefki — Klefki's Prankster gets one screen up first (priority +1), but Taunt then locks it out of its second screen, Thunder Wave, and all future status (only Foul Play remains). Houndoom Protects because Rotom-Wash Hydro Pump is a guaranteed OHKO (111.8-167.1%); Protect wastes that hit and keeps Houndoom alive for Flash Fire utility and Klefki KO threat next turn. This wins the utility war: opponent gets at most one screen, no TWave, and Rotom-Wash is trapped by Shadow Tag (only Volt Switch escapes).
decisions.notebook: G2T1: Mega Evolved Gengar, Taunted Klefki, Protected Houndoom vs predicted Hydro Pump. Mega Gengar Speed ~200 (max Speed Timid, base 130). Klefki gets one screen before Taunt lands (Prankster +1 > Taunt priority 0). Rotom-Wash Hydro Pump guaranteed OHKO on Houndoom (111.8-167.1%) — must respect this speed/damage threat whenever Rotom is active and Houndoom is on field. Houndoom Flamethrower possible OHKO on Klefki (95.1-179.5%) but not guaranteed through Light Screen. Plan: next turn chunk/KO Klefki with Houndoom Flamethrower + Gengar support, then Energy Ball Rotom-Wash. Bring Tyranitar mid-game for sand + Excadrill sweep. Watch Metagross-Mega (130-162 Spe) outspeeding Excadrill in sand (140). Dragapult (178-213) may outspeed Mega Gengar (~200) if max invested.

decisions.rationale: Fake Out fails on turn 2 (not Incineroar's first turn on field). Darkest Lariat into Gengar-Mega has a 61-117% OHKO chance and forces the opponent into a dilemma: either Protect Gengar (wasting its turn) or risk losing it. Switching Klefki to Rotom-Wash preserves the Taunted Klefki and brings in a switch-in that resists Houndoom's Flamethrower (11-27% under Light Screen) while taking manageable damage from either of Gengar's attacks (Shadow Ball 23-50%, Energy Ball 35-76%). Rotom also has Sitrus Berry for recovery. This line keeps pressure on Gengar while safely repositioning.
decisions.notebook: Game 2. Light Screen active for 7 more turns. Klefki Taunted (~2 turns remain). Incineroar's Fake Out expired. Opponent's unrevealed pair (2 of: Tyranitar/Excadrill/Gholdengo/Tauros-Aqua) still in back. Houndoom Flash Fire confirmed; never target it with Fire moves. Gengar-Mega remains the priority target for Darkest Lariat. Preserve Incineroar for Ghost-type pressure; Rotom-Wash walls Houndoom's Fire STAB and pivots with Volt Switch.

decisions.rationale: Both Pokémon are trapped by Shadow Tag. Klefki is Taunted and can only Foul Play. Darkest Lariat (61-117%) + Foul Play (17-46%) into Gengar-Mega has a high combined KO probability. If Gengar Protects, we force the Protect and Klefki absorbs Flamethrower (65-95%), but we maintain board position. If it doesn't Protect, it likely faints, freeing both from Shadow Tag. Foes outspeed us, but both our moves are independently lethal enough that even if Klefki goes down first, Incineroar's Darkest Lariat still threatens the KO.
decisions.notebook: Game 2. Light Screen 7 turns left. Klefki Taunted (~2 turns remain). Gengar-Mega Shadow Tag confirmed: traps non-Ghost foes; neither Incineroar nor Klefki can switch. Incineroar Fake Out expired. Houndoom Flash Fire confirmed. Darkest Lariat into Gengar-Mega: 61-117% (not guaranteed OHKO). Foul Play into Gengar-Mega: 17-46%. Opponent's unrevealed pair (2 of: Tyranitar/Excadrill/Gholdengo/Tauros-Aqua) still in back.

decisions.rationale: Incineroar's Fake Out is unavailable (entered turn 1, first-turn-only restriction), so its real threat is Darkest Lariat on Gengar (96.4-140.1%, possible OHKO). Combined with Klefki Foul Play (26.3-32.1%), a double-target on Gengar guarantees the KO. Gengar must Protect to survive. Houndoom Flamethrower on Klefki is 2x SE (63.4-119.7% through Light Screen with Life Orb) — big chunk or possible KO. Even if opponent reads Protect and redirects to Houndoom, both their attacks are 0.5x on Dark/Fire typing, so Houndoom survives and still fires. Both foes are Shadow Tag-trapped (no switching moves), so preserving Gengar maintains positional dominance.
decisions.notebook: G2T2: Incineroar Fake Out is dead on turn 2+ (first-turn-only). Incineroar Darkest Lariat can OHKO Mega Gengar (96.4-140.1%). Klefki Foul Play on Gengar only 26.3-32.1% (uses Gengar's low Atk). Houndoom Flamethrower on Klefki through Light Screen: 63.4-119.7% (possible OHKO with Life Orb). Gengar Shadow Ball on Klefki: only 29.9-56.8% (0.5x + Light Screen). Both opponent Pokémon trapped by Shadow Tag (no switching moves in their sets). Plan: chunk/KO Klefki this turn, then pivot to Tyranitar for sand + Excadrill sweep. Watch for Metagross-Mega (130-162 Spe) outspeeding Excadrill in sand (140). Dragapult (178-213) may outspeed Mega Gengar (200).

decisions.rationale: Klefki is Taunted, trapped by Shadow Tag, and at 18% HP — it dies this turn to any special attack from either foe. Its only possible action is Foul Play, and the only worthwhile target is Gengar-Mega (16.8–45.9%). Incineroar's Darkest Lariat into Gengar-Mega deals 61.1–117% with a solid OHKO chance; Flare Blitz is weaker (41.9–82.2%) and cannot OHKO alone. Combined damage (77.9–162.9%) gives a strong probability of removing the opposing Mega and its Shadow Tag, trading Klefki for Gengar-Mega at worst and leaving Incineroar healthy against Houndoom plus two unrevealed backs. Even if Klefki is KO'd before moving, Darkest Lariat alone still threatens the OHKO.
decisions.notebook: Game 2. Light Screen 5 turns left after this turn. Klefki Taunted (~1 turn remains). Gengar-Mega Shadow Tag confirmed. Incineroar Fake Out expired. Darkest Lariat vs Gengar-Mega: 61.1-117%. Foul Play vs Gengar-Mega: 16.8-45.9%. Opponent's unrevealed pair is 2 of: Tyranitar (SmoothRock/SandStream), Excadrill (FocusSash/SandRush), Gholdengo (Leftovers/GoodAsGold), Tauros-Aqua (SitrusBerry/Intimidate). Houndoom is Life Orb Timid Flash Fire.

decisions.rationale: Rotom-Wash is the clear switch: Hydro Pump threatens both Tyranitar (32.9-75.4%) and Houndoom (72.5-169.3%, possible OHKO), while Dragapult takes 66-97% from Houndoom Dark Pulse even through Light Screen and its attacks are all neutral or resisted. Rotom-Wash takes manageable damage (Dark Pulse 20-48%, Rock Slide 19-44%, Flamethrower 11-27%) and has Sitrus Berry recovery. Incineroar must stay in to preserve offensive pressure and avoid giving a free turn.
decisions.notebook: Game 2. Light Screen 5 turns left after this turn. Klefki fainted turn 3. Opponent's 4th unrevealed is one of Excadrill (FocusSash/SandRush), Gholdengo (Leftovers/GoodAsGold), Tauros-Aqua (SitrusBerry/Intimidate). Rotom-Wash matches up well against all three. Incineroar Fake Out window expired (entered turn 1).

decisions.rationale: Gengar switches to Tyranitar to dodge the Darkest Lariat OHKO (96.4-140.1%) and bring Sand Stream for future Excadrill sweep. Both foes are Shadow Tag trapped and can't switch; Klefki is Taunted (only Foul Play). Houndoom Flamethrower guarantees KO on 17% Klefki (63.4-119.7% through Light Screen). Worst case both foes target Houndoom: Darkest Lariat NVE 30-45%, Foul Play NVE 11-13% — Houndoom survives comfortably. If foes target Gengar, moves fail. This preserves Gengar, sets sand, and removes Klefki.
decisions.notebook: G2T3: Switching Gengar→Tyranitar to dodge Darkest Lariat OHKO and bring sand. Houndoom Flamethrower KOs Klefki (guaranteed). Plan next: Tyranitar sand + Excadrill sweep. Watch Metagross-Mega (130-162 Spe) may outspeed Excadrill in sand (140). Dragapult (178-213) may outspeed Mega Gengar (200). Incineroar Darkest Lariat OHKOs Gengar (96.4-140.1%). Houndoom Flamethrower on Klefki through Light Screen: 63.4-119.7% (guaranteed KO from 17%). Klefki Foul Play on Houndoom: only 11.2-13.2%. Incineroar Darkest Lariat on Houndoom: 30.3-44.7%. Incineroar Flare Blitz on Houndoom: immune (Flash Fire).

decisions.rationale: Hydro Pump into Houndoom threatens an OHKO (90-169%) and forces a likely Protect. If Houndoom doesn't Protect and Hydro Pump connects, we remove their special attacker immediately. Incineroar Protects to avoid the near-certain Tyranitar Rock Slide (45-63% to Incineroar), preserving its HP for later. Even if both foes attack Rotom-Wash, the worst case (Sucker Punch + Rock Slide) deals ~62% max, activating Sitrus Berry without a KO. This keeps both of my Pokémon healthy while maintaining offensive pressure.
decisions.notebook: Game 2. Light Screen has ~5 turns left. Opponent's 4th is one of Excadrill (FocusSash/SandRush), Gholdengo (Leftovers/GoodAsGold), or Tauros-Aqua (SitrusBerry/Intimidate). Rotom-Wash matches up well against all three. Dragapult is preserved for Gengar-Mega. Incineroar's Fake Out window is expired.

decisions.rationale: Houndoom is guaranteed KO'd by Rotom-Wash Hydro Pump (111.8-167.1% from 74%), so it must Protect. Tyranitar Rock Slide hits both foes with physical damage (bypasses Light Screen): 33.7-63.5% on Incineroar (SE, putting it in KO range) and 19.7-36.8% on Rotom-Wash. Even if opponent predicts Protect and double-targets Tyranitar, it survives (Hydro Pump 35.7-55.1% + Darkest Lariat 11.1-15.9% = 47-71% max HP, leaving 17-41% from 88%). This is the safest high-value play: protect the threatened slot while spreading chip to both opponents.
decisions.notebook: G2T4: Rock Slide + Houndoom Protect. Rotom-Wash Hydro Pump guaranteed KOs Houndoom from 74% (111.8-167.1%). Tyranitar survives Hydro Pump from 88% (35.7-55.1%). Incineroar Darkest Lariat on Tyranitar only 11.1-15.9%. Rock Slide on Incineroar 33.7-63.5% (SE physical, bypasses Light Screen), on Rotom-Wash 19.7-36.8% (neutral spread). Crunch on Rotom-Wash 28.7-52.8% (physical, 100% acc). Houndoom Dark Pulse on Rotom-Wash 25.5-48% (halved by Light Screen). Excadrill cannot hit Rotom-Wash (Levitate blocks HHP, Steel 0.25x, Rock Slide neutral spread). Excadrill best targets: Incineroar with High Horsepower (2x SE) or Rock Slide (2x SE spread). Plan: chip both foes this turn, next turn consider bringing Excadrill in sand to pressure Incineroar or Gengar-Mega with Shadow Tag + Energy Ball on Rotom-Wash. Watch for Metagross-Mega (130-162 Spe) outspeeding Excadrill in sand (140). Dragapult (178-213) may outspeed Mega Gengar (200).

decisions.rationale: Hydro Pump guarantees a KO on Houndoom if it stays in, removing their special attacker. If Houndoom switches, Hydro Pump still deals heavy damage to the replacement (85.7–160% into Excadrill forcing Sash, 39–70% into Gholdengo, or 24–47% into Tauros-Aqua). Darkest Lariat chips Tyranitar for 10–17% while Incineroar tanks Rock Slide comfortably behind Light Screen and Chople Berry. This preserves Dragapult in the back for Gengar-Mega and keeps the 2v1 field advantage after Houndoom is removed.
decisions.notebook: Game 2. Light Screen has ~4 turns left after this turn. Opponent's 4th is one of Excadrill (FocusSash/SandRush), Gholdengo (Leftovers/GoodAsGold), or Tauros-Aqua (SitrusBerry/Intimidate). Rotom-Wash matches up well against all three. Dragapult is preserved for Gengar-Mega. Incineroar's Fake Out window is expired.

decisions.rationale: Switch Houndoom to Gengar-Mega to bring Shadow Tag online, trapping both foes so neither can switch out. Tyranitar uses Crunch on Rotom-Wash (physical, bypasses Light Screen, 28.7–52.8%) to chip it from 68%. If the opponent targeted Houndoom with Hydro Pump (the expected play since it KOs Houndoom), the move fails because Houndoom left the field. Next turn Gengar-Mega at 200 Speed outspeeds everything and can Taunt Rotom-Wash to block Protect/Will-O-Wisp, then finish it with Shadow Ball. Houndoom is preserved at 68% for later. Main risks: Rotom targets Tyranitar with Hydro Pump instead (survives at ~33–52%) or burns it with Will-O-Wisp; Incineroar Flare Blitz on Gengar-Mega is SE on Poison but requires predicting the switch.
decisions.notebook: G2T5: Switched Houndoom → Gengar-Mega (Shadow Tag traps both foes) + Tyranitar Crunch on Rotom-Wash. Next-turn plan: Gengar-Mega (200 Spe) outspeeds all; Taunt Rotom to block Protect/Wisp then KO with Shadow Ball, or direct Shadow Ball if in range. Houndoom preserved at 68% bench. Key speed tiers: Mega Gengar 200, Dragapult 178–213 (may outspeed), Excadrill sand 140, Metagross-Mega 130–162 (may outspeed Excadrill). Excadrill cannot damage Rotom-Wash (Levitate). Opponent Light Screen 4 turns left; sand 6 turns left. Opponent 4th mon unknown from {Dragapult, Corviknight, Metagross}.

decisions.rationale: Rotom Protect shields it from Gengar's Energy Ball and Tyranitar's Rock Slide. Incineroar Darkest Lariat KOs Gengar-Mega if it doesn't Protect; if Gengar does Protect, both our Pokémon survive the turn and Gengar is forced to have burned its Protect. Either outcome preserves both our Pokémon and either removes or neutralises the opposing Mega.
decisions.notebook: Game 2. Light Screen has ~3 turns left after this turn. Opponent's 4th is one of Excadrill (FocusSash/SandRush), Gholdengo (Leftovers/GoodAsGold), or Tauros-Aqua (SitrusBerry/Intimidate). Rotom-Wash matches up well against all three. Dragapult is preserved for Gengar-Mega. Incineroar's Fake Out window is expired.

decisions.rationale: Helping Hand (priority +5) boosts Gengar's Energy Ball to a guaranteed KO (60.5-112%) on Rotom-Wash at 47%, and Gengar at 200 Spe outspeeds Rotom (106-138) so Rotom is eliminated before it can Hydro Pump Tyranitar. Incineroar's Darkest Lariat then KOs Gengar at 15% — an acceptable trade of a nearly-dead Gengar for Rotom while keeping Tyranitar at full 76%. Only risk is Rotom Protecting, but opponent has been aggressive with Hydro Pump and hasn't used Protect yet. Result: 3v2 with Tyranitar 76% + Excadrill 100% + Houndoom 68% vs Incineroar 82% + 1 unknown.
decisions.notebook: G2T6 plan: HH+Energy Ball KOs Rotom, Gengar dies to Darkest Lariat. Next: bring Excadrill (100%, Focus Sash, Sand Rush 140 Spe) into Gengar's slot. Excadrill outspeeds Incineroar and Metagross-Mega (130-162); only Dragapult (178-213) may outspeed. Excadrill Iron Head/Rock Slide/High Horsepower can sweep remaining foes. Houndoom (68%, Life Orb) on bench for Fire/Dark coverage. Opponent 4th mon unknown from {Dragapult, Corviknight, Metagross}. Sand 5 turns left after T6. Key: if opponent brings Metagross-Mega, it has Tough Claws and 130-162 Spe (slower than Excadrill 140 in sand unless high EV investment). Dragapult 178-213 is the main speed threat to Excadrill.

decisions.rationale: Gengar is fainted; bring in Excadrill (100%, Focus Sash, Sand Rush 140 Spe) over Houndoom (68%, Life Orb). Excadrill outspeeds both active foes in sand (Incineroar 80–112, Rotom-Wash 106–138) and Rock Slide hits Incineroar SE while spreading to Rotom. High Horsepower is SE vs Metagross and Incineroar (Rotom immune via Levitate). Focus Sash guarantees survival against Dragapult if it is the 4th mon. Houndoom stays as a strong bench option for later. Tyranitar stays in (Pass) to preserve sand and support next turn.
decisions.notebook: G2: Excadrill brought in for fainted Gengar. Sand 5 turns remaining (Tyranitar Smooth Rock). Excadrill 100% Focus Sash Sand Rush 140 Spe outspeeds Incineroar, Rotom-Wash, Metagross-Mega (130-162); only Dragapult (178-213) outspeeds. Rock Slide SE vs Incineroar; High Horsepower SE vs Metagross/Incineroar but Rotom immune (Levitate). Houndoom 68% Life Orb on bench. Opponent 4th mon unknown from {Dragapult, Corviknight, Metagross}. Opponent Light Screen 3 turns left. Series score 0-1, must win this game.

decisions.rationale: Excadrill outspeeds both active Pokémon under Sand Rush and OHKOs Incineroar with High Horsepower (83.2–116.8%). Switching Incineroar to Dragapult preserves Incineroar and brings in a faster mon that survives any single Excadrill hit (HH 58.2–83.6%, Iron Head 49.1–69.7%, Rock Slide 23.6–33.3%). Dragapult Fire Blast then outspeeds Rotom and breaks Excadrill's Focus Sash (min 64.5%), after which Rotom Hydro Pump finishes through the broken sash. Tyranitar's Crunch into Rotom (35–50.3%) is a threat but Rotom moves before Tyranitar if Tyranitar's Speed ≤108, which covers most of its range. Even in worst-case scenarios the position remains advantageous.
decisions.notebook: Game 2. Opponent brought Tyranitar/Excadrill/Gengar-Mega/Houndoom. Gengar-Mega fainted turn 6. Excadrill is Sand Rush + Focus Sash, the primary threat while sand is up. Dragapult preserved as late-game cleaner; Rotom-Wash has excellent matchup into Excadrill and Houndoom. Incineroar should be conserved for Houndoom and general bulk.

decisions.rationale: Excadrill outspeeds everything (280 Spe) and guaranteed KOs Incineroar with High Horsepower (77-139% vs 76% HP), removing the Flare Blitz OHKO threat before Incineroar can act. Tyranitar Crunch into Rotom-Wash deals 28.7-52.8% from its 41% HP for a possible KO; even if it survives, Rotom is at single digits and easily finished next turn. If Incineroar Protects, High Horsepower is blocked but Crunch still chunks Rotom, and Excadrill (immune to sand chip via Ground/Steel typing) survives any single hit via Focus Sash to finish Incineroar next turn. This removes the opponent's biggest threat while simultaneously pressuring their lowest-HP mon.
decisions.notebook: G2 Turn 7 plan: Excadrill HH→Incineroar (guaranteed KO, outspeeds at 280), Tyranitar Crunch→Rotom (possible KO from 41%). Excadrill Ground/Steel immune to sand chip at 1 HP. If Incineroar Protects, pivot to Rock Slide or HH next turn. Houndoom 68% on bench for late-game cleanup. Opponent 4th mon unknown from {Dragapult, Corviknight, Metagross}; Excadrill outspeeds all except none (280 > Dragapult 213). Must win G2 to extend series.

decisions.rationale: Excadrill under Sand Rush outspeeds both my Pokémon and Rock Slide KOs both. Switching Dragapult to Incineroar triggers Intimidate (-1 Atk to both foes) before any moves, letting Incineroar survive even double Rock Slide. Rotom Protect keeps it alive. Next turn Incineroar Fake Out (priority +3) flinches Excadrill while Rotom Hydro Pump KOs it, removing Sand Rush and freeing Dragapult to clean later.
decisions.notebook: Game 2. Opponent brought Tyranitar/Excadrill/Gengar-Mega/Houndoom. Gengar-Mega fainted turn 6. Excadrill is Sand Rush + Focus Sash (consumed), the primary threat while sand is up. Dragapult preserved as late-game cleaner; Rotom-Wash has excellent matchup into Excadrill and Houndoom. Incineroar should be conserved for Houndoom and general bulk. Sandstorm has ~3 turns remaining; once it ends or Excadrill falls, Dragapult becomes fastest.

decisions.rationale: Automatic: only one legal joint action.

Excadrill (Speed 280) outspeeds everything and KOs Dragapult (12%) with Iron Head (100% acc, guaranteed KO). Tyranitar KOs Rotom-Wash (1%) with Crunch (100% acc, guaranteed KO). Both are physical so Light Screen is irrelevant. If one foe Protects, the other still dies. If both Protect, I lose nothing and repeat. Worst case trades 1% Excadrill for a foe, leaving Tyranitar+Houndoom vs Incineroar — a winning endgame.
decisions.notebook: G2 endgame plan after this turn: If both foes KO'd, opponent sends Incineroar (76%). I have Tyranitar (76%) + Houndoom (68%) + possibly Excadrill (1%). Houndoom Flamethrower OHKOs Incineroar (Fire vs Fire/Dark = SE). Tyranitar can chip or Protect. If only one foe KO'd, Excadrill at 1% is expendable; clean up with Tyranitar/Houndoom. Sandstorm turns remaining matter for Excadrill's Sand Rush speed. Houndoom Flash Fire absorbs Fire moves for safe switches into Incineroar's Flare Blitz.

decisions.rationale: Fake Out (+3) KOs 1% Excadrill through resist; if Excadrill Protects (+4), Fake Out is blocked but Dragapult's own Protect (+4) shields it from Tyranitar's attack. Either way Dragapult survives the turn. Once Excadrill falls and sand ends (1 turn left), Dragapult becomes the fastest Pokémon and cleans.
decisions.notebook: Game 2, up 1-0. Opponent brought Tyranitar/Excadrill/Gengar-Mega/Houndoom. Gengar-Mega fainted turn 6. Excadrill is Sand Rush + consumed Sash, the only mon that outspeeds Dragapult in sand. Once Excadrill is removed and sand expires, Dragapult is the fastest threat. Incineroar must use Darkest Lariat into Houndoom (Flash Fire blocks Flare Blitz). Tyranitar is weak to Incineroar's Darkest Lariat and Dragapult's Thunderbolt.

decisions.rationale: Tyranitar Crunch into Dragapult is a guaranteed KO (SE, 37.9-71.2% vs 12% HP). Excadrill Rock Slide hits both foes—chips Incineroar for 20.8-36.5% SE (Chople Berry doesn't apply to Rock) while also hitting Dragapult. If Incineroar Fake Outs Excadrill (KO at 1%), Tyranitar still KOs Dragapult. If Incineroar Fake Outs Tyranitar (flinch), Excadrill Rock Slide chips Incineroar and Dragapult dies to sandstorm/Life Orb recoil. Excadrill at 1% is expendable; Rock Slide chip on Incineroar makes the Houndoom Flamethrower endgame much cleaner.
decisions.notebook: G2 endgame: After Dragapult KO'd, Houndoom Flamethrower SE on Incineroar (Fire/Dark) for cleanup. Tyranitar Crunch SE on Dragapult guaranteed KO from 12%. Chople Berry only halves SE Fighting hits, not Rock. Fake Out unavailable after Incineroar's first action turn (turn 9 is first action turn since switch-in on turn 8). Sandstorm has 2 turns left; Excadrill Sand Rush active through next turn. Houndoom Flash Fire blocks Fire attacks for safe positioning vs Incineroar Flare Blitz.

decisions.rationale: Automatic: only one legal joint action.

selection: Protect [success rate reduced: Protected last turn]
decisions.rationale: Dragapult at 6% dies to any attack; Protect gives a ~33% chance to survive since it was used last turn. Protect (+4 priority) outruns Sucker Punch (+1), so if it works both Sucker Punch and Rock Slide are blocked. Incineroar's Darkest Lariat into Houndoom chips it to 31–50%, setting up a potential KO next turn if Dragapult lives. Incineroar survives Rock Slide (29.7–42.6% from 49%) and is not threatened by a KO this turn. Flare Blitz is useless into Flash Fire Houndoom and Darkest Lariat does more than Flare Blitz into Tyranitar.
decisions.notebook: Game 2, up 1-0. Opponent brought Tyranitar/Excadrill/Gengar-Mega/Houndoom. Gengar-Mega and Excadrill fainted. Sand expires after turn 10. Dragapult is the fastest mon once sand ends. Incineroar must use Darkest Lariat into Houndoom (Flash Fire blocks Flare Blitz). Tyranitar is weak to Incineroar's Darkest Lariat and Dragapult's Thunderbolt.

decisions.rationale: Dragapult is dead this turn regardless (Life Orb recoil if it attacks, sandstorm if it Protects). Sucker Punch at priority +1 KOs Dragapult before it can fire off Thunderbolt (35-53% on Houndoom), preserving Houndoom's HP. Rock Slide hits both foes—SE on Incineroar for 24-42%, dropping it to ~6-24%. If Dragapult Protects, Sucker Punch fails but Dragapult dies to sandstorm and Rock Slide still damages Incineroar. Next turn is a trivial 2v1 vs Incineroar whose attacks are all NVE or Flash Fire-immune.
decisions.notebook: G2 endgame locked: after Dragapult dies (Life Orb/sandstorm), 2v1 vs Incineroar. Incineroar attacks all NVE/immune vs Tyranitar+Houndoom (Flash Fire blocks Fire). Rock Slide is only SE option on Incineroar. Chople Berry only halves SE Fighting, irrelevant here. Series is 0-1, must win G2 to force G3.

decisions.rationale: Dragapult is dead to any attack and Life Orb recoil; we must maximise its one move. Thunderbolt into Houndoom (28–54%) plus Incineroar Darkest Lariat (18.1–37.3%) guarantees Houndoom faints if both connect. If the opponent uses Sucker Punch, Dragapult falls before moving but Incineroar still has a ~70% roll to KO Houndoom alone. Eliminating Houndoom is the only path to a 1v1, even though Incineroar vs Tyranitar is unfavourable.
decisions.notebook: Game 2, up 1-0. Opponent brought Tyranitar/Excadrill/Gengar-Mega/Houndoom. Gengar-Mega and Excadrill fainted. Sand expired after turn 10. Dragapult is the fastest mon without sand. Incineroar cannot beat Tyranitar 1v1 without prior chip; Flare Blitz is NVE and blocked by Flash Fire on Houndoom. Darkest Lariat is the only viable attack into both foes.

decisions.rationale: Sucker Punch (priority +1) guarantees KO on 6% Dragapult before it can attack (Life Orb recoil would also KO it). Rock Slide hits both foes — SE on Incineroar for 24-42% chip, bringing it to ~6-24% for easy 2v1 cleanup. If Dragapult Protects (heavily reduced at streak 2), Sucker Punch fails but Rock Slide still damages Incineroar, and Dragapult remains stuck at 6% with no switch options for next turn.
decisions.notebook: G2 endgame locked: after Dragapult dies (Life Orb/sandstorm), 2v1 vs Incineroar. Incineroar attacks all NVE/immune vs Tyranitar+Houndoom (Flash Fire blocks Fire). Rock Slide is only SE option on Incineroar. Chople Berry only halves SE Fighting, irrelevant here. Series is 0-1, must win G2 to force G3. Opponent team for G3: Dragapult, Klefki, Incineroar, Rotom-Wash, Corviknight (Tailwind/BraveBird/Roost/Uturn, Careful, Leftovers, Mirror Armor), Metagross (MeteorMash/PsychicFangs/BulletPunch/Protect, Adamant, Metagrossite, Clear Body→Tough Claws Mega).

decisions.rationale: Incineroar is guaranteed to be outsped and OHKOed by Tyranitar's Rock Slide before it can move. Even with a Rock Slide miss (10%), neither Darkest Lariat nor Flare Blitz can KO Tyranitar from 76% HP, even with a critical hit. The game is mathematically lost. Forfeiting saves time and preserves focus for game 3 with the series tied 1-1.

decisions.rationale: 1v1 endgame: Tyranitar (76%) vs Incineroar (8%). Rock Slide is SE (2x) and guaranteed KO from 8% HP (23.8-42.4% damage) at 90% accuracy. Crunch is only NVE (0.5x, 7.9-14.7%) and not a guaranteed KO. Even if Rock Slide misses, all of Incineroar's attacks are NVE vs Tyranitar and cannot KO at 76%, giving another shot next turn. If Incineroar Protects, it resets the Protect streak and I simply try again next turn at 90%. Rock Slide maximizes win probability this turn.
decisions.notebook: G2 endgame: Tyranitar 1v1 vs Incineroar 8%, Rock Slide guaranteed KO on hit (90% acc). If win G2, G3 prep: opponent full team is Dragapult/Klefki/Incineroar/Rotom-Wash/Corviknight/Metagross. Metagross-Mega (Tough Claws, 130-162 Spe Adamant) is a major threat. Corviknight Mirror Armor punishes stat drops. Klefki Prankster screens+TWave. Consider bringing Tyranitar+Excadrill sand core + Gengar-Mega + Houndoom again, or swap Gengar for a different pick if Darkest Lariat pressure is too high.

reflections.summary: Lost because Dragapult was brought in too early and chipped into Sucker Punch range, allowing Houndoom to remove it before it could threaten Tyranitar. Incineroar was left alone against Tyranitar with no way to break through.
reflections.adjustment: Preserve Dragapult for the late game. Lead with Incineroar and Rotom-Wash to pressure sand with Fake Out and Hydro Pump, and use Klefki screens to enable Dragapult to clean up after sand sweepers are removed.

reflections.summary: Won by removing Klefki early with Taunt + Flamethrower, then grinding down the opponent's team with the sand core. Houndoom's Sucker Punch picked off Dragapult and Tyranitar's Rock Slide finished the 8% Incineroar for the 1v1 win. Gengar-Mega did its job trapping and Taunting but fell predictably to Darkest Lariat.
reflections.adjustment: Gengar-Mega is too fragile against Incineroar's Darkest Lariat; if bringing it again, keep it away from Incineroar or consider a different Mega pick. Also be ready for Dragapult double-Protect sequences—lead Sucker Punch with a different move to avoid wasted turns.
